b: For the second straight week, a youthful IM won Freestyle Friday on November 20, this time IM Sergey Sklokin-Bagiyan, whose 9.5 points were enough for outright victory. GM Jeffery Xiong finished sole second on nine points, with GMs Alexey Sarana and Benjamin Bok rounding out the top four on 8.5 points each.

With just two weeks now remaining in the Freestyle Friday Championship (FFC), Sklokin-Bagiyan now ranks in the top 12, but only the top eight will reach the 2027 Freestyle World Championship. There is currently a 10-point gap, which is what players earn for victory, between eighth and 16th place, so several players still have chances.
In the women's standings, IM Meri Arabidze finished ninth to gain the most points, adding some buffer between her and players outside the top eight.
GM Oleksandr Bortnyk, who finished fifth, played on the Freestyle Chess channel. He also observed and commentated on other games each round after his was over. You can view the stream below:

Sklokin-Bagiyan, Xiong, Sarana, and Bortnyk were among the five players to start 4/4, the fifth being GM Sina Movahed. Bok, however, lost two of his first three games before storming back into the top four. Bortnyk was already all but calling the tournament for Xiong, seeing the way his games were playing out, but only Movahed advanced to 5/5, which he did with a win over Bortnyk. Xiong and Sklokin-Bagiyan drew, as did Sarana in his fifth-round game.

Sarana went on to defeat Sklokin-Bagiyan in the sixth round, leaving the 13-year-old Armenian on 4.5/6. He was a perfect 5/5 thereafter. In the same round, Xiong defeated Movahed, joining Sarana in the lead.

In the Xiong vs. Sarana game that ensued, Xiong won to take the sole lead, seeming to bear out Bortnyk's comments. But then Bortnyk himself made the stop in the eighth round. He spent much of the game bemoaning his performance, but perked up with endgame chances and got it done. Although he went on to lose his next two games, he recovered into fifth place and earned some FFC points to extend his lead in those standings.

It was FM Artin Ashraf, another non-GM teenager like Sklokin-Bagiyan and November 13 winner IM Khuong Duy Dau, who took down Bortnyk in the ninth round. Meanwhile, Sklokin-Bagiyan was continuing his reascent into contention, joining Xiong in a share of second place with a win over Movahed. After the 10th round, that became a share of first when Xiong and Sklokin-Bagiyan both won, Sklokin-Bagiyan by delivering Bortnyk's next loss in just 25 moves. Bortnyk, already down to five seconds on his clock by move 15, just missed a fork, although his position was already difficult.

Because they had already played, Xiong and Sklokin-Bagiyan faced Bok and Ashraf, respectively, in the final round. Both games seemed headed to draws in the endgame, which very likely would have favored Xiong based on tiebreaks. But then Ashraf erred, and Sklokin took advantage, while Xiong's game did indeed end in half points.

Sarana began the round in a tie with GM David Paravyan for fifth place as the only players on 7.5/10. They were not in contention for first place, but Sarana's wild win delivered him third just ahead of Bok.

Freestyle Friday is Chess.com's weekly tournament dedicated to Freestyle Chess for titled players. The tournament begins at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time/17:00 Central European Time/20:30 Indian Standard Time.

Nathaniel Green is a staff writer for Chess.com who writes articles, player biographies, Titled Tuesday reports, video scripts, and more. He has been playing chess for about 30 years and resides near Washington, DC, USA.
